newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 4.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Energy Regulatory Board orders an increase of 50 centavos per litre in the prices of gasoline, diesel and six other oil products including fuel oil effective 6:00 a.m. on Wednesday. (ALL PAPERS)
- The satisfaction rating of President Fidel Ramos continues to get high marks, a survey by the Social Weather Station last October 5 shows. (CHRONICLE)
- Members of the House of Representatives have raised the budget allocated for themselves by 50 percent, Senator Alberto Romulo says. (INQUIRER)

- A ranking opposition leader insists that the presidential palace will continue to push for a change in the Constitution despite repeated assurance by President Fidel Ramos that he will not seek an extension of his term. (TODAY)

- A surge in Christmas spending and hike in local transporation fares are expected to drive Philippine inflation to 5.7 percent in November from 4.7 percent in October, a Reuters poll shows. (ALL PAPERS)
- Philippine Airlines cancels orders for eight Boeing 747 series 400 and four Airbus 340s after acceding to the demand of pilots to increase their salary. (MALAYA)
- The Asia's Emerging Dragon Corp decides to drop its plan to build a new terminal in the Ninoy Aquino International Airport. (BUSINESSWORLD)
